title: the beginning of weekly visual diaries
content:
weekly visual diaries

intro to a new series

when I thought about my last year, I could feel the emotional shape of months emerging in my mind — but I didn’t know where the weeks went; let alone the days. they felt blurry and slippery, like fish jumping in fog.

so, I decided to start a new project this year — at the end of each week, I’ll draw a single image to synthesize how the week felt for me. in the past I’ve drawn more infrequent, very dramatic and emotional mood diaries, but this visual diary practice will be a bit more ordinary and mundane. I’ll try not to get bored of it by the end of the year.

here’s the first one, from the week before last.

three waking times

january 13-19, 2025

it was rainy all week. I woke up between 3-5 AM several days (in a row) and worked to the disappearing moon, then robo (our robot vacuum) started at 7:30 AM. K, who is a night person, said that he wanted to wake up to a clean house…

*

technically, it was the first “settled” week I’ve had back in my work routines, in my own space, in many months. I guess my body was a little overeager to be awake in the dark. in Istanbul winters, the sun doesn’t rise until after 8:30 AM, and I often most relish the morning darkness. for me, it would be a dream to work from early dark until noon, then be done for the day.
